tools.title: Distribution Explorer
tools.whatYouTry: Switch probability families and drag mean, spread, or rate parameters to watch shape, mean, and variance shift live.
tools.whatYouChange: Distribution family and distribution parameter sliders
tools.whatYouSee: Rescaled probability density or mass bars with live mean and variance readouts
tools.ideaTaught: Each family captures a structural process with its own relationship between center and tail variance.

tryThis.prompt: Select Binomial or Poisson and compare what happens to variance as the rate climbs.
tryThis.check: For Poisson(lambda), variance rises 1-for-1 alongside the mean, widening the bell curve as counts grow.

tryThis.prompt: Pick a skewed family like Exponential and see where its mean sits compared to the peak density.
tryThis.check: Peak density sits at 0 while the right tail pulls the mean strictly higher above zero.

tryThis.prompt: Watch a symmetrical Normal curve when you double its scale parameter.
tryThis.check: Peak density drops proportionally as mass spreads further into the tails while keeping total area equal to 1.

tools.title: Bayes Belief Updater
tools.whatYouTry: Set a rare prior prevalence alongside high test sensitivity and check the true posterior after a positive result.
tools.whatYouChange: Prior P(disease), true-positive P(+|disease), and false-positive P(+|no disease) sliders
tools.whatYouSee: Side-by-side prior vs. posterior percentages and exact Bayes formula evaluation
tools.ideaTaught: Low base rates let even small false-positive rates outweigh true positives.

tryThis.prompt: Set prior P(disease) to 1.00%, true positive to 95.0%, and false positive to 5.0%. Before looking, guess whether posterior exceeds 50%.
tryThis.check: Posterior lands near 16.10% because 5% of the 99% healthy population generates roughly five times as many false alarms as true catches.

tryThis.prompt: Drop false-positive rate from 5.0% down to 0.5% while holding prior at 1.00%. Predict how much posterior jumps.
tryThis.check: Cutting false positives tenfold lifts posterior above 65%, proving false-alarm control dominates rare-event screening.

tryThis.prompt: Raise prior P(disease) from 1% to 20% at 95%/5% accuracy.
tryThis.check: With a common condition (20% prior), posterior crosses 82% because true positives outnumber healthy false alarms.

tools.title: Entropy & KL Divergence Explorer
tools.whatYouTry: Shift approximating distribution Q probabilities away from P and watch KL divergence surge when support drops.
tools.whatYouChange: Preset or slider balance between true distribution P and model distribution Q
tools.whatYouSee: Paired outcome bars alongside live H(P), H(P, Q), and D_KL(P || Q) readouts
tools.ideaTaught: Cross-entropy loss penalizes assigning near-zero probability to events that actually occur.

tryThis.prompt: Match Q closely to P first and note the minimum value of cross-entropy.
tryThis.check: When Q matches P exactly, D_KL hits 0.000 and cross-entropy equals Shannon entropy H(P).

tryThis.prompt: Starve one outcome in Q where P still puts meaningful probability.
tryThis.check: D_KL(P || Q) climbs steeply toward infinity because log(p/q) amplifies small denominators q.

tryThis.prompt: Make P nearly uniform across outcomes and observe entropy H(P).
tryThis.check: Maximum uncertainty maximizes H(P), requiring more bits per sample on average.

tools.title: 2x2 Matrix Transformation Lab
tools.whatYouTry: Drag all four matrix entries to warp the grid and watch unit basis vectors and determinant collapse.
tools.whatYouSee: Transformed grid lines, landing arrows for e1 and e2, and live det(A) area factor
tools.ideaTaught: A matrix is a linear map whose columns tell you where the standard axes land.

tryThis.prompt: Set row 1 to [1.0, 0.5] and row 2 to [2.0, 1.0]. Predict the geometric shape of the grid.
tryThis.check: det(A) hits 0.00 and the entire 2D grid collapses onto one line (rank-1 singularity).

tryThis.prompt: Flip sign on A[0][0] = -1.0 while keeping A = [[-1, 0], [0, 1]]. Notice det(A).
tryThis.check: det(A) becomes -1.00: area stays 1, but orientation mirrors across the y-axis.

tryThis.prompt: Hold A[0][1] = 0.0 and adjust A[1][0] only. Observe which basis arrow moves.
tryThis.check: Only column 1 moves (vertical shear), proving column j equals the image of basis vector j.

tools.title: CAP Partition Trade-Off Simulator
tools.whatYouTry: Trigger a network partition between replicas and toggle CP vs. AP behavior to inspect reads and writes.
tools.whatYouChange: Link partition status and consistency vs. availability preference
tools.whatYouSee: Split cluster state showing accepted vs. rejected writes and stale vs. fresh reads
tools.ideaTaught: When links stay healthy you get both C and A; during a partition you must sacrifice one.

tryThis.prompt: Test a write to the minority side under CP mode while partitioned.
tryThis.check: CP rejects the write with an error so no replica returns conflicting balances later.

tryThis.prompt: Switch the same partitioned cluster to AP mode and perform reads across both sides.
tryThis.check: Both sides respond successfully, exposing stale divergence until partition recovery reconciles writes.

tryThis.prompt: Heal the partition and check what remains of the CP vs. AP conflict.
tryThis.check: Once communication resumes, latency dominates normal operations (the PACELC trade-off).

tools.title: TCP vs. UDP Packet Loss Simulator
tools.whatYouTry: Raise simulated network packet loss and compare unordered UDP drops with retransmitted TCP arrival.
tools.whatYouChange: Simulated packet loss slider (0% to 60%)
tools.whatYouSee: 10-packet delivery strips showing gaps in UDP and complete ordered delivery in TCP
tools.ideaTaught: Ordered completeness costs retransmission delay whenever packets drop on the wire.

tryThis.prompt: Set packet loss to 0% first. Does UDP lose anything compared to TCP?
tryThis.check: All 10 packets arrive cleanly under both protocols; the difference surfaces only when packets drop.

tryThis.prompt: Drag packet loss to 40%. Guess how many of 10 UDP packets go missing and whether TCP drops any.
tryThis.check: UDP drops 4 packets permanently while TCP retransmits until all 10 land in sequence.

tryThis.prompt: Think about live voice calls vs. REST API payloads at 20% packet loss.
tryThis.check: Voice drops stale missed frames on UDP rather than stalling audio behind TCP head-of-line retransmits.

tools.title: Consensus Quorum Calculator
tools.whatYouTry: Disconnect nodes one by one in a 5-node consensus group to find the commit boundary.
tools.whatYouChange: Unreachable nodes slider (0 to 4)
tools.whatYouSee: Reachable/unreachable node statuses and majority quorum commit badge
tools.ideaTaught: Majority quorums guarantee safety because any two commit sets overlap on at least one node.

tryThis.prompt: Set Unreachable nodes to 2 out of 5. Guess if the cluster can still commit.
tryThis.check: Yes: 3 of 5 reachable meets the majority floor(5/2) + 1 = 3 threshold.

tryThis.prompt: Increase Unreachable nodes from 2 to 3.
tryThis.check: With only 2 nodes reachable, quorum fails immediately and commits halt to prevent split-brain writes.

tryThis.prompt: Calculate why a 4-node cluster still only tolerates 1 failure rather than 2.
tryThis.check: With 4 nodes, majority is floor(4/2) + 1 = 3, giving no extra fault tolerance over a 3-node group.

tools.title: Async Event Loop Timeline
tools.whatYouTry: Compare blocking sequential calls against single-threaded async task switching over multiple I/O awaits.
tools.whatYouChange: Execution pattern toggle (Sequential vs. Async concurrent)
tools.whatYouSee: Task timeline showing overlapped network wait intervals and total elapsed latency
tools.ideaTaught: asyncio wins on concurrent I/O waits, not by adding extra CPU cores.

tryThis.prompt: Run sequential execution over 3 I/O waits and note total wall time.
tryThis.check: Total wall time equals the sum of every wait interval sequentially.

tryThis.prompt: Switch to concurrent asyncio gather mode and compare the bar length.
tryThis.check: Total time collapses toward the single slowest I/O call because waiting overlaps inside one thread.

tryThis.prompt: Ask what happens if one task replaces await sleep with a pure Python CPU loop.
tryThis.check: A tight synchronous loop starves the single event loop and stalls every co-scheduled task.

tools.title: Threading vs. Multiprocessing Explorer
tools.whatYouTry: Flip between CPU-bound and I/O-bound workloads across Python threads and OS processes.
tools.whatYouChange: Workload type (CPU-bound vs. I/O-bound) and execution model (threading vs. multiprocessing)
tools.whatYouSee: Effective completion time bar across 4 workers and GIL contention note
tools.ideaTaught: Pick threading when waiting on sockets/files, and multiprocessing when burning CPU cycles.

tryThis.prompt: Select CPU-bound with threading. Predict whether 4 threads run near 100ms or 400ms.
tryThis.check: Close to 380ms: the GIL serializes Python bytecode across threads even on multi-core hardware.

tryThis.prompt: Switch the CPU-bound workload to multiprocessing.
tryThis.check: Runtime plunges to ~140ms as each process owns its own GIL on a separate CPU core.

tryThis.prompt: Now select I/O-bound with both models and inspect the difference.
tryThis.check: Threading hits ~105ms without multiprocessing startup and pickle serialization overhead (~130ms).

tools.title: Generator vs. List Memory Curve
tools.whatYouTry: Scale dataset size up to 20,000 items and watch eager lists climb past constant-memory generators.
tools.whatYouChange: Dataset size slider (100 to 20,000 examples)
tools.whatYouSee: Log-scale memory curves comparing O(N) list RAM against flat O(1) generator yield RAM
tools.ideaTaught: Lazy generators stream huge training datasets using only one item's RAM at a time.
tools.learnTitle: Language Fundamentals: OOP, Functional & Modern Python

tryThis.prompt: Slide Dataset size down to 500 examples. Notice how small both lines sit.
tryThis.check: At 500 items, the list uses ~24.4 MB vs. 0.049 MB for a generator—safe until corpus sizes grow.

tryThis.prompt: Pull Dataset size to 20,000 and watch the red list curve vs. the flat generator line.
tryThis.check: List RAM climbs past 976 MB while generator memory remains locked at ~0.049 MB.

tryThis.prompt: Notice why log scale hides part of how dramatic that linear slope looks visually.
tryThis.check: A generator pipeline keeps memory bounded even if the input file streams millions of records.

tools.title: Linear Regression Studio
tools.whatYouTry: Drag slope w and intercept b to minimize MSE by hand, flip an outlier on, or run batch gradient descent.
tools.whatYouChange: Mode, noise, outlier toggle, slope w, intercept b, learning rate, and dataset seed
tools.whatYouSee: Vertical error bars, fitted regression line, and gradient descent trajectory on the loss contour
tools.ideaTaught: Squared loss amplifies distant outliers and over-large learning rates explode along the quadratic bowl.

tryThis.prompt: In Fit It Yourself mode, tune w and b until MSE bottoms out, then toggle Outlier: On.
tryThis.check: The single extreme outlier generates a disproportionately long residual that pulls the optimal slope sharply.

tryThis.prompt: Switch to Gradient Descent Lab at default learning rate and press Step 5 times.
tryThis.check: Steps descend rapidly along the steep w axis first before drifting toward the valley floor.

tryThis.prompt: Push learning rate upward until the trajectory oscillates across the contour.
tryThis.check: Exceeding the curvature stability threshold makes MSE diverge rather than settle.

tools.title: Logistic Regression Studio
tools.whatYouTry: Compare Cross-Entropy against naive MSE gradient descent when starting confident in the wrong direction.
tools.whatYouChange: Mode, noise, weight w, bias b, and Cross-Entropy vs. MSE loss selector
tools.whatYouSee: Sigmoid probability curve, vertical 0.5 boundary, and optimization path over the loss surface
tools.ideaTaught: Sigmoid saturation stalls MSE gradients on confident errors whereas Cross-Entropy stays linear.

tryThis.prompt: In Fit It Yourself mode, set w near 0. Predict what happens to the decision boundary slope.
tryThis.check: Predicted probabilities flatten toward a constant everywhere, failing to separate class 0 from class 1.

tryThis.prompt: Switch to Gradient Descent Lab with Cross-Entropy selected and step from the bad start.
tryThis.check: Gradients stay strong enough to swing w and b rapidly across the decision boundary.

tryThis.prompt: Reset GD and switch Loss to MSE (naive). Run the same steps.
tryThis.check: Sigmoid derivative saturation stalls progress on confident wrong points in a flat plateau.

tools.title: Decision Boundary Playground
tools.whatYouTry: Test k-NN, SVMs, and Decision Trees on spirals and moons while dialing complexity up and down.
tools.whatYouChange: Dataset pattern, model family, complexity hyperparameter (k / C / gamma / depth), and noise
tools.whatYouSee: 2D class decision regions alongside live train vs. test accuracy
tools.ideaTaught: Excess capacity memorizes training noise into jagged islands that hurt test generalization.

tryThis.prompt: Pick k-NN on a noisy dataset with k = 1, then raise k toward 15.
tryThis.check: k = 1 carves tiny isolated noise pockets (high variance) while larger k smooths boundaries.

tryThis.prompt: Switch to Linear SVM on a Spiral dataset.
tryThis.check: A straight hyperplane cannot untangle spirals regardless of C without kernel features.

tryThis.prompt: Switch to RBF SVM and test very high gamma vs. moderate gamma.
tryThis.check: Extreme gamma wraps tight circles around individual training dots, causing test accuracy to drop.

tools.title: Lasso Regression Studio
tools.whatYouTry: Increase L1 regularization lambda and watch correlated and noise features drop cleanly to exact zero.
tools.whatYouChange: Regularization lambda, correlation (x1, x2), noise, and New Dataset seed
tools.whatYouSee: Coordinate-descent weight path chart, per-feature readouts, MSE, and dropped count
tools.ideaTaught: The L1 penalty produces sparse models by snapping small weights to exact zero.

tryThis.prompt: Push lambda slowly upward from 0.00. Predict which feature gets marked (dropped) first.
tryThis.check: Noise feature x3 hits exact 0.000 earliest, followed by weak feature x4 while strong predictors survive.

tryThis.prompt: Raise Correlation (x1, x2) near 0.96 and watch both correlated coefficients as lambda rises.
tryThis.check: Lasso tends to keep one of the correlated pair alive while pushing its redundant partner to zero.

tryThis.prompt: Watch MSE immediately after x3 drops to zero.
tryThis.check: MSE barely shifts when dropping truly irrelevant predictors—showing sparse pruning without accuracy loss.

tools.title: Neural Network Playground
tools.whatYouTry: Build hidden layers from scratch, change activations and learning rates, and watch training carve curves live.
tools.whatYouChange: Dataset shape, hidden layer counts/widths, activation, learning rate, and Play/Step
tools.whatYouSee: 2D output heatmap, live train/test loss curves, and weight connection widths
tools.ideaTaught: Non-linear activations let stacked linear layers fold input space around spirals and XOR rings.

tryThis.prompt: Select the XOR or Spiral dataset with Linear activation only and press Play.
tryThis.check: Regardless of depth, Linear networks can only learn a single straight boundary line.

tryThis.prompt: Switch activation to ReLU or Tanh with 2 hidden layers and restart training.
tryThis.check: Loss drops steadily as folded half-planes stitch into curved multi-region boundaries.

tryThis.prompt: Test a tiny network vs. wide layers with L2 regularization on noisy data.
tryThis.check: Too little capacity underfits while unchecked capacity overfits noise pockets unless regularized.

tools.title: Gradient Descent Optimizer Race
tools.whatYouTry: Race SGD, Momentum, RMSProp, and Adam across narrow ravines and saddle plateaus.
tools.whatYouChange: Loss surface, learning rate, momentum, and active optimizer selection
tools.whatYouSee: Synchronized 2D contour trajectories, step counts, and running loss readouts
tools.ideaTaught: Per-parameter adaptive scaling and momentum calm oscillation across elongated loss valleys.

tryThis.prompt: Pick an elongated valley/ravine and run plain SGD vs. Momentum at the same learning rate.
tryThis.check: SGD zigzags perpendicular to the narrow walls while Momentum cancels oscillation and shoots along the canyon.

tryThis.prompt: Compare SGD against Adam on a saddle plateau.
tryThis.check: Plain SGD stalls near flat gradient zones where adaptive normalization keeps Adam moving.

tryThis.prompt: Push learning rate upward on Momentum and observe overshooting.
tryThis.check: Accumulated velocity can carry the iterate past the minimum into spiral oscillations.

tools.title: Attention Step-Through Explorer
tools.whatYouTry: Step from QKV projections through scaled dot-products and softmax to watch contextual token mixing.
tools.whatYouChange: Active Query token, step (Q/K/V -> Scores -> Scale -> Softmax -> Weighted V), and prompt
tools.whatYouSee: Projection matrices, unscaled vs. scaled logits, probability weights, and updated output vector
tools.ideaTaught: Scaling by sqrt(d_k) keeps dot-product variance near 1 so softmax gradients stay healthy.

tryThis.prompt: Select a pronoun token like 'it' and watch the Softmax step.
tryThis.check: Weight concentrates sharply onto its antecedent noun rather than averaging neighboring words equally.

tryThis.prompt: Compare Scores before and after dividing by sqrt(d_k).
tryThis.check: Division compresses extreme raw dot products away from near-one-hot softmax saturation.

tryThis.prompt: Step to Weighted V and check how output changes for two distinct query tokens.
tryThis.check: Each output row blends value vectors in proportion to its own normalized attention weights.

tools.title: Diffusion Forward Noising Lab
tools.whatYouTry: Scrub diffusion timestep t from clean data toward T and track remaining signal vs. added Gaussian noise.
tools.whatYouChange: Diffusion timestep slider t (and noise schedule progression)
tools.whatYouSee: Corrupted signal samples alongside signal sqrt(alpha_bar) and noise sqrt(1 - alpha_bar) shares
tools.ideaTaught: Closed-form forward schedules jump directly to any noise level t in one step during training.
tools.learnTitle: Generative Models: GANs, Diffusion and Flow Matching

tryThis.prompt: Hold t at step 0 first and inspect the noise fraction.
tryThis.check: Signal coefficient equals 1.00 and data structure remains completely uncorrupted.

tryThis.prompt: Drag t halfway across the schedule.
tryThis.check: Local fine modes blur together while coarse global clusters remain faintly distinguishable.

tryThis.prompt: Push t to the maximum step and check the final distribution.
tryThis.check: All structure vanishes into pure unit Gaussian noise regardless of starting shape.

tools.title: Embedding Space Explorer
tools.whatYouTry: Probe nearest neighbors and vector arithmetic analogies across semantic word clusters.
tools.whatYouChange: Selected query word, analogy presets, and similarity readout
tools.whatYouSee: 2D semantic map, ranked cosine neighbor table, and parallelogram analogy offset vectors
tools.ideaTaught: Co-occurrence structure encodes shared concepts and relational shifts as vector offsets.

tryThis.prompt: Inspect the nearest neighbors for an animal or royalty term before trying analogies.
tryThis.check: Tight semantic clusters share high positive cosine scores (~0.7+) despite differing character spelling.

tryThis.prompt: Run the analogy vector king - man + woman.
tryThis.check: Adding the gender offset lands closest to queen in embedding coordinates.

tryThis.prompt: Compare two completely unrelated concepts on opposite clusters.
tryThis.check: Cosine similarity drops near zero or below, showing near-orthogonal feature directions.

tools.title: Tokenization Ambiguity Inspector
tools.whatYouTry: Compare subword vs. character and whitespace splits across edge cases like whitespace, code, and numbers.
tools.whatYouChange: Example category or tokenizer split granularity
tools.whatYouSee: Highlighted token boxes showing how seemingly identical strings yield very different token IDs
tools.ideaTaught: Models never read characters; subtle leading-space or digit splits alter sequence math.
tools.learnTitle: Classical NLP: Tokenization, POS Tagging, NER & Parsing

tryThis.prompt: Compare a standalone word vs. the same word preceded by a space or punctuation.
tryThis.check: They map to distinct subword token IDs unless normalization strips leading spaces.

tryThis.prompt: Inspect multi-digit numbers across tokenizers.
tryThis.check: Irregular 2- or 3-digit chunking explains why plain LLMs struggle to count digits reliably.

tryThis.prompt: Observe compound words or code identifiers vs. common English words.
tryThis.check: Rare terms fragment into multiple short pieces, multiplying context token cost.

tools.title: BLEU N-Gram Precision Explorer
tools.whatYouTry: Test Exact match, Valid paraphrase, and Word salad against a fixed reference sentence.
tools.whatYouChange: Candidate translation selector (Exact match, Valid paraphrase, Word salad)
tools.whatYouSee: Unigram precision, bigram precision, and combined geometric-mean BLEU percentages
tools.ideaTaught: Surface n-gram metrics penalize fluent paraphrases while higher-order n-grams catch scrambled word order.

tryThis.prompt: Pick 'Valid paraphrase' ('a cat was sitting on the mat') vs. reference ('the cat sat on the mat'). Guess BLEU.
tryThis.check: BLEU drops far below 100% despite preserving complete meaning because exact lexical stems changed.

tryThis.prompt: Now select 'Word salad' ('the mat sat on the cat'). Compare unigram vs. bigram precision.
tryThis.check: Unigram precision sits deceptively at 100%, while bigram precision collapses to catch the scrambled order.

tryThis.prompt: Check why BLEU combines multiple n-gram orders via geometric mean rather than unigrams alone.
tryThis.check: Any zero higher-order overlap pulls the geometric product down hard.

tools.title: 2D Convolution Sliding Window
tools.whatYouTry: Step a 3x3 filter across an image grid and toggle edge vs. blur kernels to read each dot product.
tools.whatYouChange: Kernel preset and receptive-field position step
tools.whatYouSee: Highlighted 3x3 input window, kernel weights, element-wise sum, and output feature pixel
tools.ideaTaught: A convolution shares one small local detector uniformly across every spatial offset.

tryThis.prompt: Place a vertical edge filter over a uniform bright or dark patch. Predict the output dot product.
tryThis.check: Left positive weights and right negative weights cancel out to ~0 across flat regions.

tryThis.prompt: Slide the same edge kernel right across a sharp dark-to-light vertical boundary.
tryThis.check: Dot product peaks strongly, lighting up only along pixels straddling the edge.

tryThis.prompt: Switch to a smoothing box or Gaussian blur kernel over a single bright pixel.
tryThis.check: Energy spreads across adjacent neighbors while reducing peak contrast.

tools.title: Image Tensor RGB Explorer
tools.whatYouTry: Inspect how visual pixels turn into Height x Width x 3 integer grids across R, G, and B channels.
tools.whatYouChange: Pixel or channel view toggle
tools.whatYouSee: Rendered bitmap next to raw [R, G, B] matrix slices
tools.ideaTaught: Vision models ingest numeric H x W x C arrays where brightness and hue split per channel.

tryThis.prompt: Inspect a pure gray or white pixel's RGB numbers.
tryThis.check: Equal values across R, G, and B produce neutral luminance with zero color tint.

tryThis.prompt: Check a bright warm yellow or orange patch across the three channel grids.
tryThis.check: Red and Green channels carry high values while Blue drops near zero.

tryThis.prompt: Count how tensor memory multiplies between single-channel grayscale and RGB.
tryThis.check: Color images triple first-layer parameter dimensions compared with H x W x 1 grayscale.

tools.title: Morphological Operations Grid
tools.whatYouTry: Apply Erosion, Dilation, Opening, and Closing to a binary mask containing a hole and a noise speck.
tools.whatYouChange: Operation selector (Original, Erosion, Dilation, Opening, Closing)
tools.whatYouSee: 11x11 binary grid updating blob thickness, center hole size, and isolated noise speck
tools.ideaTaught: Opening erases isolated noise without shrinking shapes; Closing fills holes without growing noise away.

tryThis.prompt: Compare Erosion vs. Original around the isolated pixel at top-right and the hole inside the 7x7 square.
tryThis.check: Erosion erases the isolated speck immediately, shrinks the blob, and widens the inner hole.

tryThis.prompt: Select Opening (Erosion then Dilation). Does the noise speck return?
tryThis.check: No: once erased by erosion, zero pixels have nothing to dilate back, yet the main blob returns to size.

tryThis.prompt: Switch to Closing (Dilation then Erosion) and inspect both the center hole and top-right speck.
tryThis.check: Closing seals the small inner hole permanently, though the isolated speck shrinks back to a blob rather than disappearing.

tools.title: Sampling & Nyquist Aliasing Lab
tools.whatYouTry: Lower sample rate relative to tone frequency and watch fake low-frequency aliasing appear.
tools.whatYouChange: Tone frequency vs. sampling rate slider
tools.whatYouSee: True wave, sample timestamps, and reconstructed aliased curve below 2 * f_max
tools.ideaTaught: Discretizing audio requires sampling strictly above twice its highest frequency (Nyquist rate).

tryThis.prompt: Set sample rate clearly above twice the signal frequency (f_s > 2f).
tryThis.check: Discrete sample points capture every peak and trough cleanly enough to recover the true tone.

tryThis.prompt: Drop sample rate below 2f and trace the curve connecting sample dots.
tryThis.check: A phantom lower-frequency wave emerges through the same points—irreversible aliasing distortion.

tryThis.prompt: Notice why human audio tops at ~20 kHz while CDs sample at 44.1 kHz.
tryThis.check: Sampling at > 2 * 20 kHz leaves headroom for anti-aliasing filters before digitizing.

tools.title: Fourier Sum-of-Sines Synthesizer
tools.whatYouTry: Add odd harmonics k <= 1 through k <= 25 and watch sine sums converge into a sharp square wave.
tools.whatYouChange: Harmonics included pills (k <= 1, 3, 5, 9, 15, 25)
tools.whatYouSee: Reconstructed time-domain waveform plus individual odd-harmonic frequency bars 4/(k*pi)
tools.ideaTaught: Any periodic signal decomposes cleanly into weighted pure sinusoids in frequency space.

tryThis.prompt: Select k <= 1 first.
tryThis.check: A single fundamental sine wave covers the rough period with no sharp corners.

tryThis.prompt: Step up to k <= 9 and inspect the flat top vs. sharp vertical jump.
tryThis.check: Adding higher-frequency odd multiples flattens the plateau and sharpens the vertical transition.

tryThis.prompt: Click k <= 25 and look closely at the sharp step corners.
tryThis.check: Persistent overshoot ripples remain right at each discontinuity—Gibbs phenomenon from sharp step truncation.

tools.title: CTC Frame Alignment & Collapse
tools.whatYouTry: Inspect frame-level acoustic emissions with '-' blanks and trace how CTC preserves double letters.
tools.whatYouChange: Phrase selector ("HELLO" vs. "SPEED")
tools.whatYouSee: Per-frame acoustic stream, duplicate-merged strip, and final blank-stripped transcript
tools.ideaTaught: Collapsing duplicates before stripping blanks lets unaligned ASR models distinguish 'LL' from 'L'.

tryThis.prompt: Look at frames 7 to 12 in "HELLO" (L, L, -, L, L). Predict what happens after merging consecutive duplicates.
tryThis.check: The single '-' blank breaks the L run into L - L so dropping blanks afterward keeps both L's intact.

tryThis.prompt: Imagine if CTC stripped '-' blanks BEFORE merging duplicates on "HELLO".
tryThis.check: The model would erroneously collapse "HELLO" into "HELO".

tryThis.prompt: Switch to "SPEED" and spot the exact blank separating double E's.
tryThis.check: Multiple frames emit '-' in the middle, letting stretched vowels align freely to two distinct letters.

tools.title: LLM Inference Flow Visualizer
tools.whatYouTry: Step through autoregressive generation stages and adjust softmax temperature from deterministic to creative.
tools.whatYouChange: Pipeline step selector, temperature slider, and prompt preset
tools.whatYouSee: Prefill vs. decode execution phases, token probability distribution, and sampled word trace
tools.ideaTaught: Prefill runs parallel across all prompt tokens while decode runs sequentially one token per step.

tryThis.prompt: Lower temperature toward minimum during the decoding step.
tryThis.check: Softmax concentrates nearly all mass onto the top logit, collapsing sampling toward greedy argmax.

tryThis.prompt: Raise temperature noticeably and compare the tail token bars.
tryThis.check: Low-probability candidates gain real sampling odds, raising variance and novelty.

tryThis.prompt: Compare prefill vs. decode stage workloads across the same prompt.
tryThis.check: Prefill evaluates the whole input matrix at once while each decode step generates strictly one token.

tools.title: RAG Pipeline Simulator
tools.whatYouTry: Adjust chunk sizes, overlap, top-k retrieval, and query wording to see grounded answers pass or break.
tools.whatYouChange: Chunk size, chunk overlap, top-k selector, and query input
tools.whatYouSee: Split document boundaries, similarity rankings, retrieved context snippets, and simulated output
tools.ideaTaught: RAG errors stem mostly from missing retrieval recall or broken chunk splits before the LLM runs.

tryThis.prompt: Shrink chunk size very low with zero overlap on a multi-sentence fact.
tryThis.check: Key context splits across two disconnected fragments, lowering similarity and cutting evidence mid-thought.

tryThis.prompt: Set top-k = 1 on a query requiring two facts in different paragraphs.
tryThis.check: Top-k = 1 misses the supporting half even when embeddings ranked both near the top.

tryThis.prompt: Add overlap and raise top-k slightly, then inspect retrieved tokens.
tryThis.check: Context completeness recovers, at the cost of extra input tokens passed to generation.

tools.title: KV Cache Computation Counter
tools.whatYouTry: Switch Naive vs. KV cache over 5 generated tokens and count total K/V projections performed.
tools.whatYouChange: Mode toggle (Naive no cache vs. KV cache) and generated tokens slider (1 to 5)
tools.whatYouSee: Step-by-step recomputed vs. cached token grid and cumulative K/V projection counter
tools.ideaTaught: Caching prior K/V tensors slashes prefix projection growth from O(T^2) down to O(T).

tryThis.prompt: Set Generated tokens to 5 in Naive mode and read total computations.
tryThis.check: Total hits 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 = 15 recomputations because every old token gets projected again at each step.

tryThis.prompt: Toggle to KV cache at 5 tokens.
tryThis.check: Total drops cleanly from 15 down to 5 because only the single newly emitted token projects fresh K and V.

tryThis.prompt: Watch the highlighted red squares vs. cached squares as step t climbs.
tryThis.check: Notice that KV caching saves projection FLOPs at the price of storing cached keys and values in GPU VRAM.

tools.title: BM25 Term Saturation & Length Lab
tools.whatYouTry: Vary term frequency, k1 saturation, document length, and b normalization to inspect live BM25 terms.
tools.whatYouChange: Term frequency tf, saturation k1, doc length |D|, and length norm b sliders
tools.whatYouSee: TF saturation curve and live IDF, B length factor, TF factor, and total score formula
tools.ideaTaught: BM25 saturates repeated keywords cleanly via k1 and normalizes long documents via b.

tryThis.prompt: Keep k1 near 1.2 and push term frequency tf from 1 to 20. Guess whether score doubles tenfold.
tryThis.check: Score plateaus quickly below an asymptote—repeating a word 20 times barely outscores 5 clean mentions.
